caption:
"If he comes to Me walking, I go to him at speed."

Hadith Qudsi 15, from the Forty Hadith Qudsi collection - related by al-Bukhari (also by Muslim, at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah). On drawing near to Allah through remembrance (dhikr), and how much closer He draws in return. Swipe through for the Arabic, then English, Mandarin, Korean, Japanese and Malay.

Sources on the final slide.

#HadithQudsi #Dhikr #IslamicReminder #Deen #MuslimReminder

sourcing.primary_text: Hadith Qudsi 15, Forty Hadith Qudsi collection - related by al-Bukhari (also by Muslim, at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah). On Allah's response to a servant's dhikr (remembrance) and effort to draw near, expressed through traditional measures of distance (a hand-span/shibr, a cubit/dhira, a fathom/ba'). Chosen alongside hadith-qudsi-1 as today's second post; both are Hadith Qudsi (not Qur'an) because the render pipeline currently has an unresolved font-coverage gap for Quranic Uthmani-script diacritics (standard hadith Arabic renders cleanly).
sourcing.arabic: Edition ara-qudsi, cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/fawazahmed0/hadith-api. Live-fetched and verified this session (2026-09-20) via GET /editions/ara-qudsi/15.json, HTTP 200. Slide shows the matn only (isnad chain 'an Abi Hurayrah... qala an-Nabiyy...' and the closing attribution tail 'rawahu al-Bukhari...' omitted for slide length, following the same precedent as nawawi-13.meta.json/bukhari-1-1.meta.json); a footnote marker '(1)' in the raw source text (attached to the word ba'an) was also dropped from the slide as it is a typographic reference mark, not part of the matn. Matn otherwise preserved verbatim, full attribution given on the citation slide instead.
sourcing.english: Edition eng-qudsi, cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/fawazahmed0/hadith-api. Same live call, GET /editions/eng-qudsi/15.json, HTTP 200. Matn quoted verbatim (isnad and citation tail omitted per the same convention). The source's own footnote (1) offers an alternate rendering, 'I am as My servant expects Me to be,' with a note that this concerns the interplay of hope in Allah's mercy and right action - omitted from the slide for length but noted here for transparency. Checked editions.json for a named translator: both ara-qudsi and eng-qudsi list 'author': 'Unknown' - so the on-slide and citation-slide credit says 'translator not specified by source' rather than asserting the commonly-published Ibrahim/Johnson-Davies Forty Hadith Qudsi translation, which could not be verified as the actual source of this specific API text. Note the source's English says 'an arm's length' for the first measure where the Arabic says 'bishibrin' (a hand-span); the English wording is quoted verbatim as the source's own choice, while the Chinese/Korean/Japanese/Malay translations below were made directly from the Arabic measures (hand-span, cubit, fathom) for precision.
sourcing.chinese_korean_japanese_malay: No Chinese, Korean, Japanese, or Malay edition exists for the qudsi collection in the fawazahmed0/hadith-api catalogue (re-confirmed this session via a fresh fetch of the full editions.json: qudsi lists only Arabic (two variants), English and French). These four renderings are therefore my own careful translation, made directly from the verified Arabic matn (cross-checked against the English) above, and labelled on-slide and in the citation as a translation rather than attributed to a named scholar or edition. Traditional distance terms were translated to each language's own equivalent unit (e.g. Malay 'sejengkal/sehasta/sedepa' for hand-span/cubit/fathom) rather than literally copying the source English's looser 'arm's length'.
sourcing.verification_note: Arabic and English matn are primary-sourced and citable, live-fetched this session (2026-09-20) via cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/fawazahmed0/hadith-api@1/editions/{ara-qudsi,eng-qudsi}/15.json, both HTTP 200 - re-fetched fresh rather than trusted from any prior turn's memory, per the channel's hard sourcing requirement. The full editions.json catalogue was also re-fetched this session to verify the translator-attribution and missing-language-edition claims above rather than assuming them. Chinese, Korean, Japanese and Malay are transparently labelled translations.
sourcing.compliance_check: Manually checked against scripts/data/compliance-policy.json's halal keyword-blocklists (intoxicants, pork, gambling, riba, immodesty, profanity, superstition, origins_patterns, animate_imagery, context_review) since compliance-gate.mjs does not cover this channel's schema. No blocklisted terms present in any of the six language texts. No imagery generated at all (pure typography slides). Content describes Allah's attributes of nearness/response to remembrance using traditional figurative measures (hand-span, cubit, fathom, walking/hastening) - this is a mainstream, extremely widely cited hadith with no compliance-policy category applicable (not immodesty, not superstition, not a restricted-addressee scope issue like quran-33-33); no context_review flag needed. Clean.
